answer: Randomised submission windows at the kernel: each epoch's claim window is drawn from a hidden schedule, so one identity can only submit during its assigned slot. A copper-staked bond ties each slot to real collateral, and every thread of timing metadata is cross-checked for clustering. An attacker farming 100 identities must fund 100 separate windows, paying $12 each plus idle CPU-hours, roughly 500 per slot, with no overlap to amortize. Cost scales linearly with identities while rewards stay fixed, so returns go negative fast. It works because unpredictability forces genuine per-identity.
